Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioner case is as Follows:

sentences.text: That on 15.08.2023 at about 05.15 PM., petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider along with her minor children Sahana, Shashank in the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-50- EF-7005 on BB Road, which was driven by her husband Gopal, near Honda Show room, Devanahalli town, wherein the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-03-MR-7636 drove it in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life with high speed and suddenly taken U turn and dashed to the motor cycle and caused the accident and thereby petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
She was shifted to Chiguru hospital, later shifted to Manasa Hospital, wherein she took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuries and she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- for her treatment.
3. Petitioner stated that she is 28 years of age working as a Tailor and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month,

Further she stated that the accident has occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.175/2022 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

She alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.

4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they have appeared through their counsel and filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire version of the petitioner in toto.

Respondents contended that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the motorcycle and respondent No.1 has contended that the insured has violated the policy conditions and there is no negligence on the part of the insurer and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. Petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and doctor as PW.2, produced and marked 17 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 17 and they are fully cross examined.

6. Respondent no.1 examined its official as RW-1, and responded No.2 examined himself as RW.2,
they produced and marked 2 documents which are at Ex.D1 and 2 and they are fully cross examined.
7. I have heard the arguments from both the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

Counsel appearing for respondent no.2 relied on the following authority:
1. The Branch Manager, ICICI Lombard Nibaye Vadde GIC ltd., VS Pooja and others.

sentences.text:
Counsel appearing for respondent No.1 has relied on the following authorities:
1. Venkataramanappa Vs Srinivas and 10 others - Gayathri vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63666978/
2 MFA No.8009/2002- Hon'ble High court of Karnataka order dated 13.01.2006.
2.

entities.text: Venkataramanappa Vs Srinivas and 10 others - Gayathri vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: SLP (S)No.8269/2025, Hon'ble Supreme court of India, order dated 20.05.2025.
8. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 15.08.2023 at about 05.15 PM., petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA- 50-EF-7005 on BB Road, near Honda Show room, Devanahalli town, wherein the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-03-MR-7636 drove it in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life with high speed and suddenly taken U turn and dashed to the petitioner motor cycle and caused the accident and thereby petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether respondent No.1 proves that respondent No.2 has violated the policy conditions as contended in the written statement?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.What order or award?
9.

After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1: In the affirmative Issue no.2: In the negative Issue no.3: In partly affirmative Issue no.4:
As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, 2 IMV reports, wound certificate, Final report, discharge summary, notice and reply which are at Ex.P.1 to 11.
11.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that respondent No.2 is the owner and the driver of the offending vehicle.

Ex.P9 is the reply given by the responded No.2,
wherein he admitted that he was driving the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident and he was having no valid driving license.

In the cross-examination of PW-1 She clearly denied the Gayathri vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63666978/
3 suggestion that her husband was alcoholic and accident occurred due to his negligence.

entities.text: Gayathri vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW-1 admitted that respondent No.2 has paid partial medical bills amount in Manasa Hospital as per Ex.D3.
She repeatedly deposed that she and her husband along with their two minor children were moving on the two wheeler and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the respondent No.2.
in the cross examination of PW-1, respondent No.2 suggested that he had paid partial amount to the hospital as per Ex.D3.
The aforesaid fact establishes that respondent No.2 has admitted his guilt and his liability.
Respondents have failed to improbabilise the allegation made by the petitioner and fails to probabilise their contention.

12. The final report filed by the investigating officer which is at Ex.P8, where in the jurisdictional police have registered the case against the respondent No.2 and it establishes that respondent No.2 has contravene the section 3 of IMV Act.
The aforesaid facts establishes the involvement of the aforesaid vehicle and the actionable negligent acts of respondent No.2 in the accident.

The final report which is at Ex.P8 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved.

13. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary as per Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.11, the entry therein shows that the petitioner has sustained grievous injury that is fracture of her right radius bone, and petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient in Manasa Hospital for a day.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

14. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
15.
Petitioner took treatment at Manasa hospital.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the fact that she has sustained the injuries in the alleged accident and he took treatment for the same.
Inasmuch, discharge summary and the medical reports issued form the hospital has to be accepted.
Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for a day, and she has spent Rs.13,436/- for treatment as per Ex12.

Further for attendant charges, transportation,
nourishing food, she might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore I award Rs.3,000/- in addition to the actual medical expenses.
In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.16,436/-.
Loss of income during laid up period.
16. The petitioner has not substantiated her nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place on 15.08.2023, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2023 is Rs.16,000/-, and same is assessed and considered as her monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least 15 days she has lost her income.
Therefore I award Rs.8,000/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

Gayathri vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63666978/
4 17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has examined the doctor B.N.Nagaraj as PW-2.
He deposed that, petitioner has 11% of whole body disability as per Ex.P16.
Learned advocate for the respondents argued that the assessment of PW-2 is on higher side.

I have perused the evidence of PW-2 wound certificate,
discharge summary given by both the hospitals, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctors who have treated her in both the hospitals.
It is true that petitioner sustained the grievous injuries that is right radius bone fracture, further doctor has admitted that fracture is united.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity due to accidental injuries is different from the percentage of physical disability due to accidental injuries.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 7%.
The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,000/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 28 years as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.15.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "17".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows; Rs.16,000/-(Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 17 ( Multiplier) X7%
(Functional Disability) = Rs.2,28,480/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.2,28,480/- as compensation under this head.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
18.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, she might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries she has forgone certain amenities available for her.
There fore I award Rs.3,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
19.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for her before accident.
Therefore I award Rs.3,000/- as compensation under this head.
20. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl Particulars Amount  No.
 1 Towards attendant charges, Rs.16,436/-
 transportation, nourishing food  2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 8,000/-

3 Loss of income on account of Rs.2,28,480/-
 permanent disability  4 pain & sufferings Rs. 3,000/-
 5 loss of amenities Rs. 3,000/-
 6 TOTAL Rs.2,58,916/-

Less amount paid by the respondent  No.2 as per Ex.D3. Rs.1,400/-
 Total Rs.2,57,516/-

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
22. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, respondent No.2 has admitted that he is having no valid license as on the date of the alleged accident.
The aforesaid fact establishes that respondent No.2 has intentionally violated the policy conditions and liability cannot be fastened on the insurer that is respondent No.1.

The learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 argued that respondent No.2 being the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, he cannot seek pay and recovery in view of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka that is Venkataramanappa Vs Srinivas and 10 others - MFA No.8009/2002- Hon'ble High court of Karnataka order dated 13.01.2006.

entities.text: Venkataramanappa Vs Srinivas and 10 others - MFA No.8009/2002- Hon'ble High court of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel appearing for respondent No.2 has not placed any contrary authority for the same.

With great respect to the aforesaid authorities and by considering the principle laid down therein and by considering the facts and attending circumstances and the conduct of respondent No.2, this Tribunal is of firm conclusion is that the Respondent No.2 is the liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent No.2 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 the affirmative, issue No.2 in the negative and issue no.3 in partly affirmative.
23. Issue No.4:

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.2,57,516/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, Cash shirestedar is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioner through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
